topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the topic of complement, setting pedagogical expectations and framing the scope of the lecture.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals, nomenclature, and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles, naming conventions, and central role of C3 cleavage in complement function.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways that initiate complement and converge to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary downstream outcomes of complement activation, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the regulatory mechanisms and surface proteins that prevent complement from attacking host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It analyzes how genetic or acquired deficiencies in various complement components lead to specific clinical phenotypes.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It explores the mechanisms pathogens employ to evade complement destruction, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus adaptations.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with closing remarks and a preview of the upcoming topic.
